requirements.title: A waitlist for full sailings
requirements.ask: When a sailing is full, let a passenger join a waitlist and be offered a seat if one frees up.
requirements.criteria: When a sailing is full, a passenger can join its waitlist. A freed seat is offered to the first on the list for 15 minutes, then to the next. A passenger sees their place in the list.

requirements.title: Free cancellation within 24 hours
requirements.ask: Let people cancel for free if they booked by mistake.
requirements.criteria: A booking cancelled within 24 hours of being made, and more than 48 hours before departure, is refunded in full. Other cancellations follow the fare rules. The receipt says which rule applied.

requirements.title: Group bookings
requirements.ask: Groups should be able to book together.
requirements.criteria: One booking can hold up to 12 passengers on one sailing. Seats are kept together when the map allows; otherwise the booking says they are apart before payment.

requirements.title: Accessible seating requests
requirements.ask: Passengers need to be able to ask for accessible seating.
requirements.criteria: A passenger can request an accessible seat or a wheelchair space while booking. The request reaches the crew list for that sailing. A sailing with no space left says so before payment.

requirements.title: Text message reminders
requirements.ask: Remind people by text before they sail.
requirements.criteria: A passenger who gives a phone number gets one text 3 hours before departure, and one if the sailing is delayed by more than 20 minutes. Texts are sent through a new messaging provider.

architecture.title: Move bookings from SQLite to Postgres
architecture.now: Bookings live in one SQLite file on the booking server. Backups are a nightly copy.
architecture.proposal: Bookings move to a managed Postgres. The booking server connects through one pool. Backups are the provider's point-in-time recovery. The SQLite file is kept read-only for 30 days.

architecture.title: An event bus between booking and payments
architecture.now: The booking service calls the payments service directly and waits for the answer.
architecture.proposal: Booking publishes a booking-made event on a new message bus; payments consumes it and publishes payment-taken. Both services stop calling each other.
